question: Which law states that a compound always contains the same elements in the same proportion by mass?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of Definite Proportions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Law of Definite Proportions**, also known as the **Law of Constant Composition**, was proposed by **Joseph Proust** in **1799**.
 
• This law states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in a **fixed ratio by mass**, regardless of the source or how the compound is prepared.
 
• The law applies to pure chemical compounds, ensuring that the proportion of elements remains consistent. For example, in water (H₂O), the ratio of hydrogen to oxygen by mass is always **1:8**.
 
• It is an essential principle in **stoichiometry**, the calculation of reactants and products in chemical reactions.
 
• This law is foundational to modern chemistry, as it establishes the concept that compounds are made of elements combined in specific proportions, laying the groundwork for the development of chemical formulas and molecular theory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass:**

 
 
• Proposed by **Antoine Lavoisier** in **1789**, it states that **mass is neither created nor destroyed** in a chemical reaction.
 
• This law is fundamental to balancing chemical equations and understanding that the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products.
 
• Example: In the reaction between hydrogen and oxygen to form water, the total mass of hydrogen and oxygen is equal to the mass of water produced.
 
 
 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions:**
 
 
• Proposed by **John Dalton** in **1803**, it states that when two elements form more than one compound, the ratios of the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in **small whole numbers**.
 
• Example: Carbon and oxygen form two compounds: carbon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂). The ratio of oxygen masses in CO and CO₂ is 1:2.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro’s Law:**
 
 
• Proposed by **Amedeo Avogadro** in **1811**, it states that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain an equal number of molecules.
 
• This law is critical to understanding the behavior of gases and is the basis for the concept of the **mole** in chemistry.
 
• Example: One mole of any gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP) occupies a volume of **22.4 liters**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of the Law of Definite Proportions:**
 
 
• The law is used in determining the **empirical formula** of compounds.
 
• It helps in **quality control** during the synthesis of chemical compounds.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in **analytical chemistry**, ensuring the purity of chemical substances.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Law of Definite Proportions** applies only to **pure substances** and not to mixtures.
 
• This law is sometimes considered a precursor to the modern atomic theory, as it implies that matter is composed of discrete units (atoms).
 
• Joseph Proust’s experiments with compounds like copper carbonate and tin oxides demonstrated the consistency of element ratios, providing empirical evidence for this law.
 
• While the law is universally true for chemical compounds, exceptions can occur in non-stoichiometric compounds, where the ratio of elements can vary slightly.
